facts.fact: The Ministry of Lands says the UgNLIS, rolled out nationally between February 2015 and February 2020, is a computerized system through 22 Ministry Zonal Offices that reduces the time to check, update and transfer land.
The Ministry of Lands says the UgNLIS is being enhanced under the NaLISEP project run from October 2023 to May 2024 by IGN FI with World Bank support.
The Ministry of Lands says the DeSINLISI national roll-out fully integrated land registration, land administration, surveying and mapping, physical planning and property valuation in the UgNLIS.

systems.platform: IGN FI consortium, World Bank funded
systems.owner: Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development

facts.fact: The Monitor reports that Uganda's digital land registration system, UgNLIS, is in service and processes transactions, with 12,748 registered transactions and thousands pending at the Jinja zonal office.
The Monitor quotes the Jinja Registrar of Titles saying digital mapping links titles to surveys, though physical verification is still needed where maps differ.

systems.owner: Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development

note: Integration with URA is stated for payment receipts only, not land tax.

facts.fact: Uganda's Ministry of Finance reforms tracker, confirmed 11 August 2026, says the National Land Information System (UgNLIS) has been upgraded and is operational in 22 zonal offices, with expansion to all land offices in progress.

systems.owner: Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development

facts.fact: Lands Permanent Secretary Okalany said the digitalised system handles land acquisition, transfer, surveying and planning, with titles processed within ten days when documents are in order.

note: No join to survey maps or valuation, or to tax, is stated.
UgNLIS is named only as used for land verification; processing of transactions is not stated.

facts.fact: IGAD says Uganda's Land Information System is in service, interoperable with physical planning, land administration, valuation, surveys and mapping, and land registration.
IGAD says Uganda's Land Information System is interoperable with land valuation, surveys and mapping.
IGAD says Uganda's Land Information System integrates land records with taxation (Uganda Revenue Authority).

facts.fact: The Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development opened an e-GP tender (closing 2 December 2026) for a consultancy to advise on and supervise the upgrade of the Uganda Land Information Management Solution (UGNLIS) using blockchain and AI.
